question.text: All $x$ satisfying the inequality $\left(\cot ^{-1} x\right)^{2}-7\left(\cot ^{-1} x\right)+10>$ 0 , lie in the interval :

solution.text: $\left(\cot ^{-1} x\right)^{2}-7\left(\cot ^{-1} x\right)+10>0$ $\left(\cot ^{-1} x-5\right)\left(\cot ^{-1}-2\right)>0$ $\cot ^{-1} x \in(-\infty, 2) \cup(5, \infty)$ But $\cot ^{-1} x$ lies in $(0, \pi)$ Now, from equation (1) $\cot ^{-1} x \in(0,2)$ Now, it is clear from the graph $x \in(\cot 2, \infty)$
